strengths: The paper addresses an important question: which latent information multimodal contrastive learning can recover when modalities have distinct latent variables and nuisance factors.

The experimental scope is substantial, including synthetic distributional misspecification, multiple CLIP encoders and shot counts, ImageNet distribution shifts, and adaptation across 11 datasets. Synthetic experiments include three repetitions.

The proposed postprocessing is simple and reports potentially useful improvements. For example, PCA plus FastICA raises the ViT16 two-shot average target accuracy from 32.51% to 37.13%. CelebA traversals also suggest some interpretable representation directions.
weaknesses: The central proofs depend on a false optimality lemma (Appendix D.1, Lemma 5.1). The normalized population contrastive loss need not have minimum zero: when the density ratio is representable, its optimum is -2 I(x;t), and the spherical vMF setting admits such an example. Furthermore, requiring paired representations to be equal almost surely under the full-support latent conditional forces constant representations, contradicting the simultaneous uniformity requirement. This invalidates the argument used to remove nuisance variables and equate the encoders in Theorems 4.1 and 4.3.

The convex-body proof incorrectly treats p(z_t) as exactly uniform in Eq. (43). Lemma 4.2 only establishes a limit as lambda approaches zero; at finite positive lambda, boundary-dependent normalization generally makes this marginal nonuniform. Consequently, the exact symmetric cross-entropy reduction and subsequent identifiability claim are unsupported. Corollary 4.4 also omits the L_alpha, alpha != 2 restriction introduced in Appendix E.2; arbitrary norms do not imply permutation-only ambiguity.

The FastICA justification in Section 5 is incompatible with the uniform hypersphere assumption. Spherical coordinates are statistically dependent through the fixed-norm constraint, and rotational symmetry prevents identification of a preferred ICA basis. Having M-1 intrinsic degrees of freedom does not establish independent sources recoverable by linear ICA. The alternative local-isometry argument for convex bodies likewise provides no demonstrated recovery guarantee for CLIP.

The downstream experiments do not isolate disentanglement from dimensionality reduction and whitening. Appendix K uses different output dimensions for ICA and PCA-plus-ICA, without matched PCA-only or whitening controls. After whitening, the orthogonal ICA rotation preserves dot-product similarities and the optimum of L2-regularized logistic regression. These controls are therefore essential to establish whether the reported gains have anything to do with the recovered independent directions.

The evidence for latent recovery is insufficient. Appendix K regresses learned representations on ground-truth factors; a rank-deficient linear projection can achieve R² = 1 while discarding factors. Predicting ground-truth factors from learned representations on held-out data and checking invertibility would address this issue. The CelebA evaluation relies on selected traversals and attribute counts, without quantitative disentanglement measurements or equivalent raw-CLIP/PCA decoder controls. These observations cannot validate real-world identifiability.

The causal contribution is insufficiently established. An undirected dependence between two latent variables describes an observational coupling, but the paper supplies no intervention semantics or identified causal query. The linear and permutation identifiability machinery is substantially inherited from Zimmermann et al. [67], making a correct multimodal extension essential to the claimed novelty.

Reproducibility and statistical reporting are incomplete. Downstream tables and curves lack uncertainty estimates. Appendix K omits synthetic sample counts, network widths, optimizer settings, and training duration; the selection protocol for PCA/ICA component counts is also unclear. No code link is supplied. These omissions make the reported robustness and practical gains difficult to assess independently.
